title: Microkernel prefetch fieldnotes — Week of 2027-11-15
content:
Fieldnotes summary (informal):

What this doc is: quick, on-the-ground notes from the microkernel prefetch work this sprint. Think of this as the team’s scratchpad + meeting minutes — rough but actionable.

Meeting context:
- Weekly sync: Mon 2027-11-15 10:00 PT (30m) — pairing with Kernel, SRE and Metrics.
- Attendees: Aisha (notes), Miguel (kernel lead), Priya (kv-cache), Evan (bench/infra), Jonah (oncall drop-in).

High-level status:
- Prefetch prototype (kernel-side async prefetch pass) is feature-complete in branch feature/microkernel-prefetch-3. Small perf wins locally, unstable in mixed-traffic canary.
- KV cache shadowing experiment continues on canary fleet (10% traffic). Hit-rate improved for prefix-heavy chat traces but tail latency regressed in 95th for long-context flows.

Quick numbers (canary -> 72h window):
- Baseline p50/p95 generation latency: 46ms / 340ms.
- Canary (prefetch enabled): p50/p95: 42ms / 370ms.
- KV cache hit ratio (end-to-end tokens): baseline 68%, canary 74% (improvement concentrated on short-turn dialogues).
- CPU on host + kernel thread delta: +6% nominal; GPU utilization unchanged.
- Mem overhead: +120MB per worker due to prefetch buffers (we expected ~100MB).

What we tried this week (experiments & outcomes):
1) Aggressive lookahead prefetch (lookahead=64 tokens)
   - Good: single-request latency for next-token samples dropped by ~4ms p50.
   - Bad: p95 increased in mixed loads due to contention on the kernel prefetch queue. Backed down.
2) Prefetch backpressure (soft drop policy)
   - Introduced a 10ms queue-time cap; requests beyond that skip prefetch. Reduced p95 regression by ~30ms, lost ~2% predicted hit ratio.
3) Selective prefetch on short-turn sessions
   - Enabled by session length heuristic (<= 8 tokens so far). Gave most of the hit-rate benefit with less tail impact. This is our current default.
4) KV shadow-mode with metric shims
   - No customer-visible writes. Collected shadow hit/miss + KV load patterns for long-context flows; surfaced correlations between large prompt prefixes and prefetch thrash.

Open issues / blockers:
- Long-context flows (>=2048 tokens) cause prefetch buffer thrash under bursty traffic. Need a better eviction/backpressure policy that accounts for sequence-length distribution.
- Kernel queue priority: prefetch work currently at same priority as scheduling; should be deprioritized under load. PR #6421 implements a priority flag but needs perf validation.
- Memory accounting: integration with agent-level telemetry missing; we should attach prefetch buffer usage to the per-request trace in tracing pipeline (OTel span).

Decisions made this week:
- Roll forward selective-prefetch-by-session-length to 50% of canary hosts for another week to collect more long-context examples.
- Keep prefetch soft-drop (10ms cap) in place; tune later if queue-depth increases.
- Defer aggressive lookahead (64 tokens) until priority scheduling is in place.

Action items (owner — ETA):
- Miguel: push PR for kernel prefetch priority flag + unit tests. ETA: 2027-11-19. (GH: #6421)
- Priya: add sequence-length histogram to kv-cache dashboards and annotate CHANGES.md with eviction heuristics for prefetch. ETA: 2027-11-18.
- Evan: run 24h canary with selective-prefetch at 50% hosts and collect full traces for >=2048 token flows; produce artifact in S3 under s3://redwood-inference/experiments/prefetch/sprint-54/. ETA: 2027-11-17.
- Aisha: draft runbook blurb for oncall describing how to toggle prefetch (runtime flags + emergency rollback). ETA: 2027-11-16.

Notes to self / quick ideas:
- Could we tie prefetch aggressiveness to recent L2 cache miss rates (host-level metric)? If kernel sees rising misses, reduce lookahead.
- Consider hybrid prefetch: kernel does cheap metadata prefetch (KV key existence, small headers) and only schedules heavier value-prefetch when host CPU availability is above threshold.
- Small thought: add a per-model config knob so large-context models default to conservative prefetch.

Post-mortem sketch if things go wrong (short):
- Symptom: p95 spikes on canary -> revert selective-prefetch config then reduce canary to 5% and open a mitigations ticket.
- Quick rollback: runtime flag PREFETCH_MODE=none; restart workers via batch restart script (playbook link in linked_artifacts).

Meeting highlights / decisions for product/security:
- No customer-facing change needed; this stays internal for now. Security reviewed the prefetch buffer growth and signed off on memory limits (security comment: avoid exposing host addresses in KV metadata returned in prefetch).

Next week plan (high level):
- Stabilize priority scheduling PR and run perf regression suite across representative models.
- Complete telemetry attachment (trace + mem) so every prefetch buffer shows up in request traces.
- Iterate on eviction heuristics: prototype LRU+size-aware eviction and simulated workload tests.

Random log excerpts from today's debug session (raw):
- "prefetch queue depth: 102 (host 3) -> consumer lag 18ms -> backpressure triggered"
- "session 0x8f4a7 leak: prefetch-buffer=1.3MB, seq-len=4096, triggered eviction"
- "canary trace id 33af: hit-predict 0.72 -> observed 0.69 (mismatch due to throttled prefetch)"

Questions for next sync:
- Are we comfortable with the memory-per-worker bump? What SLA headroom do we have in Dedicated pools? (CC: infra)
- If the priority flag shows regression, do we prefer a small hardware/instance class bump for canary hosts to increase headroom or continue software-only mitigations?

If you read only one thing: selective prefetch by session-length + 10ms soft-drop is the current safe default. It's giving most of the hit-rate wins without the big tail regressions.

Attachments & references:
- Perf runs: s3://redwood-inference/bench/prefetch/canary-2027-11-15/
- Kernel PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/6421
- Jira: ENG-1289 (prefetch priority scheduling)

End of fieldnotes. — Aisha
